name: Microcystic Lymphatic Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Lymphatic Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of soft, compressible, non-tender, multiloculated cystic masses typically present at birth or early childhood
MRI or ultrasound showing microcystic lesions with multiple small cysts (<2 cm) without solid components
Histological confirmation showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells
Exclusion of venous or combined vascular malformations by imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus imaging findings consistent with microcystic lymphatic malformation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is confirmatory but not always required if clinical and imaging findings are definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Soft, compressible, multiloculated microcystic cutaneous lesions
Persistent lymphatic fluid leakage or oozing from skin lesions
searchTerms: ongoing lymph fluid leakage from skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-pulsatile, non-tender swelling with ill-defined borders

common.symptomName: Recurrent cellulitis or localized infections in affected area
Pain or discomfort due to lesion expansion or secondary infection
searchTerms: pain from lesion infection or expansion

common.symptomName: Functional impairment depending on lesion location (e.g., restricted joint movement)
searchTerms: loss of function in affected area

occasional.notes: Lymphatic system considered part of immunological system for this profile
searchTerms: fluid buildup in limb from lymph blockage

occasional.symptomName: Compression symptoms on adjacent structures (e.g., airway obstruction if cervical)

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to intracranial microcystic lymphatic malformations
searchTerms: brain symptoms due to small cysts
nerve issues from intracranial lymphatic lesions

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure due to extensive lymphatic malformations
searchTerms: heart failure from large lymphatic growths
heart strain due to lymphatic malformations

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated inflammatory markers during infection
Lymphatic fluid analysis showing proteinaceous fluid with lymphocytes
imaging: MRI demonstrating multiloculated microcystic lesions with fluid signal intensity
Ultrasound showing multiple small anechoic cysts without flow on Doppler
CT scan may show low-density cystic masses without solid enhancement
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Histopathology showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by flat endothelial cells
Absence of arterial or venous malformations on vascular imaging

distinguishingFeatures: Slow flow venous channels on Doppler ultrasound
Mixed vascular components (capillary, lymphatic, venous) on imaging and histology
Presence of palpable thrill or bruit in some cases
More complex lesion morphology compared to isolated microcystic lymphatic malformation

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of lesion with pain or erythema indicating infection or hemorrhage
Airway compromise due to cervical or facial lesion expansion
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular anomalies classification: recommendations from the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
Alomari AI. Lymphatic malformations: diagnosis and management. Semin Intervent Radiol. 2011;28(3):274-283.
